sources.excerpt: Blackstone Appliances MOSFET Overdrive 2S Pedal Review: Honest, In-Depth Analysis | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Blackstone Appliances MOSFET Overdrive 2S Pedal Review: Honest, In-Depth Analysis By nina-harper June 4, 2026 Blackstone Appliances MOSFET Overdrive 2S Pedal Review The Blackstone Appliances MOSFET Overdrive 2S is a compact, hand-wired, true-bypass analog overdrive pedal designed to deliver responsive, amp-like saturation with dynamic touch sensitivity — not high-gain distortion. It excels in low-to-mid gain blues, classic rock, and clean boost applications, particularly when paired with tube amps. While its $229–$249 US street price sits above entry-level pedals, its discrete MOSFET circuitry, component-level transparency, and nuanced EQ control justify the cost for players prioritizing organic response over versatility. This Blackstone Appliances MOSFET Overdrive 2S pedal review examines how it performs across studio, live, and home settings — with no marketing gloss, just measurable behavior, tonal trade-offs, and clear use-case guidance. About Blackstone Appliances MOSFET Overdrive 2S Pedal Review Blackstone Appliances is a small U.S.-based boutique pedal builder founded by engineer and guitarist Mark A. Blackstone in 2012. Operating out of Portland, Oregon, the company focuses exclusively on discrete analog circuits — no op-amps or digital signal processing — emphasizing component selection, hand-soldered point-to-point wiring (on select models), and rigorous bench testing. The MOSFET Overdrive 2S (released in early 2021) evolved directly from their original MOSFET Overdrive (2015), incorporating user feedback around headroom, midrange articulation, and input impedance stability. Unlike many modern overdrives that emulate specific vintage pedals, the 2S aims to function as a transparent, expressive extension of the player’s guitar-and-amp relationship — replicating how a cranked tube preamp responds to pick attack, volume knob adjustments, and string dynamics. Its design philosophy centers on dynamic interaction , not preset tones. First Impressions Unboxing reveals a matte black, powder-coated aluminum enclosure measuring 4.75″ × 2.5″ × 1.75″ — slightly larger than a standard Boss unit but smaller than most full-size boutique pedals. The chassis feels dense and rigid (3.2 oz / 91 g), with recessed, knurled metal knobs (Volume, Tone, Drive, and a unique four-position Mode switch). The footswitch is a heavy-duty, gold-plated, soft-click momentary switch with tactile feedback and zero wobble. Input/output jacks are top-mounted, angled 90°, and soldered directly to the PCB — no chassis-mounted jack adapters. The LED is warm white, unobtrusive, and located beside the footswitch. There are no battery access points; power is DC-only (9–18V, center-negative), with no internal battery compartment. Setup requires only a 9V supply (though higher voltage yields measurable headroom gains — see Specs section). No manual is included; a downloadable PDF is available on Blackstone’s site, featuring schematics, biasing notes, and recommended pairings. Detailed Specifications Blackstone publishes complete electrical specs on its website 1 . Below is a breakdown with practical context: Power Requirement: 9–18V DC, center-negative (regulated); current draw: 7.5 mA at 9V, 9.8 mA at 18V. Higher voltage increases headroom and transient clarity without altering core voicing — verified via oscilloscope measurement of clipping threshold shift (+2.1 dBu at 18V vs. 9V). Circuit Topology: Discrete, Class-A biased, dual-MOSFET (2N7000 and BS170) front-end stage feeding passive tone stack and buffered output. No op-amps, diodes, or clipping LEDs in the signal path. Input Impedance: 1.2 MΩ (measured at 1 kHz). Matches passive single-coil pickups well; minimal high-end roll-off even with long cable runs (>25 ft). Output Impedance: 500 Ω (buffered). Blackstone Appliances builds the MOSFET Overdrive as their flagship design. Using MOSFET transistors rather than typical diode clipping, it achieves amp-like response with exceptional touch sensitivity. The circuit compresses and saturates like a pushed tube amp, cleaning up beautifully with guitar volume changes. Two modes provide different gain structures. High and low switches shape the frequency response. A longtime favorite among players seeking transparent, amp-like overdrive that responds to playing dynamics.
